name: RNR — RAR Nightly Review
tagline: What landed on the front page of the agentic web, and what broke getting there.
_note: Sources and thumbs resolve RELATIVE TO THIS FILE'S URL, so this channel plays from any host or mirror. Adding an episode means one entry in this array plus `python3 build.py` — the landing page, per-episode share and embed pages, and the RSS feed are all generated from here. Episodes are dated snapshots: the numbers on screen were true in the registry at record time and are deliberately not retconned later.

videos.title: The release couldn't be cut — and the health check had been dead for 82 days
videos.description:
A release was requested. Pre-flighting the gates locally first turned up two failures that had nothing to do with the release, and following them led somewhere worse: the nightly health check had failed 60 times in a row, last green on 11 May.

The check was broken. Not the thing it checks.

Gated agents record _stub_sha256. The integrity audit read _sha256, which is absent on those agents, then formatted its own error message with the missing key and died on a KeyError before it could print why. A second scanner was still banning exec() — a rule the registry had deliberately retired in favour of tagging it as a declared capability.

Then the check itself turned out to be incapable of failing. It ran the suite as `pytest … | tee log`, so the pipeline exited with tee's status, which is always zero. The entire suite could be red and nightly would still report green. Its registry rebuild ran on a shallow checkout, so all 278 agents came back stamped with a single commit and today's date — provenance, fabricated.

Twelve defects fixed, 51 hermetic tests added to CI, and nightly went green for the first time since May.

One decision is left, and it is not a technical one.
